newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's Yeltsin wants CIS to meet on Afghanistan.
newsitem.headline: Russia's Yeltsin wants CIS to meet on Afghanistan.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin proposed on Tuesday that leaders of the Commonwealth of Independent States should meet to discuss the situation in Afghanistan, the presidential press office said.

It said in a statement that Yeltsin, who is in hospital preparing for heart surgery, had told Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin to contact other leaders of the 12-member group created on the ashes of the Soviet Union, but set no date for the proposed meeting.
Yeltsin's press service did not say where the meeting would be held.
Russia has described the latest offensive by Afghanistan's Taleban grouping, which seized the capital Kabul last Friday, as a development which could lead to a "national catastrophe".

Moscow has also said it is worried that the upsurge of fighting in Afghanistan could make the situation worse in the former Soviet republic of Tajikistan, where the pro-Moscow government opposes Afghan-based islamic guerrillas.
Soviet troops invaded Afghanistan in 1979 but Moscow withdrew the troops almost 10 years later after they failed to put down guerrilla resistance.
